Subject: Dedicated capacity demo request — EmberTech

Hi Marissa,

We just completed the self-serve signup and indicated interest in a Dedicated capacity demo for production inference. A few quick details about our workload:
- Use case: real-time customer support summarization + agent assist (generation + short context history)
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~20 req/s, peak bursts up to 80 req/s
- Typical request size: 512 tokens (prompt + expected response ~300 tokens)
- Target: p95 tail latency < 300ms for generation at peak; need predictable throughput and predictable billing for budgeting

Would love to schedule a 45–60min demo that focuses on Dedicated capacity, autoscaling behavior, and latency/throughput tuning. Please include someone from the SE/infra side.

Thanks,
Mike Sullivan
Head of AI Platform, EmberTech

Marissa, Ava — Tue 12/1 10:00 PST works for us, confirmed.

Quick answers and additional context (I'll populate the spreadsheet after sending this):
- Steady: ~20 req/s (most requests are generation for 300 tokens). Peak bursts: up to ~80 req/s for short windows (5–10 minutes) during product launches.
- Traffic pattern: predictable spikes at 10am daily and larger spikes on release days.
- Our primary question is how Dedicated capacity handles short bursts without large latency degradation. We're also curious about using prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt structures.

Also: do you support canary/gradual rollouts of model changes on Dedicated? We need safe rollouts for model updates.

Hi Mike — looking forward to the call. A few quick notes ahead of the demo:

- Short answer on bursts: Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity and autoscale policies; for the traffic profile you described we'll show an example config that maintains p95 latency under burst when using burst capacity + pre-warmed instances.
- Cache: prefix/KV caching works well for repeated prompt templates; we typically demo response cache hit/miss and how it impacts token cost and latency.
- Canary rollouts: yes — we support canary and gradual traffic shifting between model versions on Dedicated, with automatic fallback policies.

Pre-demo checklist (please try to provide if possible):
- The filled capacity_requirements.xlsx (concurrency, token percentiles)
- One or two representative prompts (sanitized) we can use in the perf run
- Any internal compliance questions (we can include our security slides if needed)

I'll prepare a short perf scenario to mirror your 300-token generation with bursts. If the spreadsheet isn't ready, we'll run a generic perf run and discuss mapping results to your numbers.

On Tue 12/1 10:00 PST I'll share a brief dashboard and run a live scenario. Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
